headline: Indonesia's Mosques Become Earthquake Early Warning System
meta_description: A five-year pilot project in Indonesia is repurposing mosque loudspeakers as earthquake early warning systems, potentially saving lives in seconds.
summary_short: Indonesian and Japanese researchers are testing whether the country's hundreds of thousands of mosque loudspeakers can alert communities to earthquakes before shaking ar…
body:
Indonesia's hundreds of thousands of mosques may soon serve double duty: calling people to prayer and warning them of earthquakes bearing down within seconds. A five-year pilot project running until 2030 is testing whether loudspeakers already maintained by mosque communities can be connected to seismic sensors to broadcast alerts before ground shaking arrives. Several mosques have already been equipped with the system. The project emerged from a tragic observation—a 2009 earthquake in western Sumatra killed at least 1,000 people—and the conviction that even five to ten seconds of warning could save lives if the information reaches people reliably.

The genius of this approach lies in infrastructure that already exists and is tested daily. Unlike mobile phone networks that can fail during earthquakes, mosque loudspeakers are maintained by the communities they serve, making them resilient where modern systems fracture. Dr. Inoue Hiroshi of Kyoto University's Disaster Prevention Research Institute conceived the idea while researching those Sumatran earthquakes nearly two decades ago. "Every community has a mosque," he explained, and the speakers are "maintained by the people."

But the project reveals a deeper challenge: those precious few seconds demand tailored guidance. Standard international earthquake advice—drop and cover under a table—was written for well-constructed buildings. In Indonesia, many homes are built from unreinforced masonry that collapses under stress, and residents often survive by running outside. The research team is now running simulations and human experiments to develop survival guidance grounded in how Indonesian buildings actually fail. The approach is already spreading: Uzbekistan announced a similar pilot program this year to install alarm devices in 272 mosques for floods, mudflows, landslides, and avalanches.
quick_facts: Five-year pilot project in Indonesia testing mosque loudspeaker earthquake alerts until 2030
Villages 50 kilometers from earthquake epicenter may have only 5-10 seconds warning time
Mosque speakers maintained five times daily by communities who depend on them
2009 Sumatra earthquake killed at least 1,000 people, inspiring the project
Uzbekistan launched similar pilot with 272 mosques for flood and landslide warnings
